findings.title: Push notifications silently disabled by iOS 'Allow Notifications' setting
findings.description: Customer stopped receiving push notifications (session reminders, coach messages) to her phone for about a week to ten days, causing her to miss a coaching session. In-app notifications (bell icon) were still generated and present, and in-app notification preferences were all enabled. Troubleshooting found the iPhone's OS-level Settings > BetterBark > Notifications > 'Allow Notifications' toggle was switched off, blocking delivery to the device. Turning it back on (plus banners/sounds/badges) and sending a test notification confirmed the fix; both parties agreed this was a device-side setting, not a product defect, and no ticket was filed.
findings.quote: So I stopped getting notifications from the app. Session reminders, messages from my coach, all of it. Nothing's coming through to my phone.
findings.severity_reason: Root cause was confirmed as a customer-device OS setting with a known, quick self-service fix (re-enable OS notification permission); not a product defect and no product-side impact remains.
findings.match_note: Resembles no tracked issue (PROJ-160 covers iOS logout after OS update, a different symptom/root cause); explicitly resolved as an OS-level permission the user/customer's device had turned off, not a BetterBark app defect.

findings.title: Customer asked whether a missed session (caused by the notification issue) counts as a no-show penalty
findings.description: After the notification issue was diagnosed, the customer asked whether the coaching session she missed last week (due to not getting a reminder) would count against her account as a no-show penalty. Support checked and confirmed no penalty was flagged on her account for that session; it simply shows as not held.
findings.quote: the missed session from last week, is that going to count against me somehow? A no-show penalty or anything?
findings.severity_reason: Purely an account-status inquiry, immediately answered with no adverse finding; not a product defect or feature request.
findings.match_note: No related tracked issue; this is an account-policy question, not a product bug or capability gap.

findings.title: Customer requested written troubleshooting steps to share with her office about the notification toggle
findings.description: After the fix was confirmed, the customer asked Ravi to send her the step-by-step notification-permission troubleshooting instructions so she could circulate them to colleagues at her 35-person branch, suspecting others may have hit the same accidentally-disabled OS toggle. This is a request for support documentation/steps related to the notification issue already discussed, not a separate product problem.
findings.quote: Actually, send me those steps if you can, I bet other people in my office have accidentally done the same thing.
findings.severity_reason: A documentation/support request tied to the already-resolved notification issue, not a product change.
findings.match_note: Directly tied to the notification permission issue at L16; recorded as a workaround/support-material request rather than a separate ticket.
